cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Retirement ≠ career – the act of leaving one's job and ceasing to work permanently.

p.em: Example: Early retirement requires disciplined financial planning.

cosy-blockquote.p: Financial security ≠ debt – the condition of having steady income to support standard living.

p.em: Example: Achieving financial security takes decades of effort.

cosy-blockquote.p: Pension plan ≠ loan – an arrangement to provide an income when a person stops working.

p.em: Example: Company pension plans vary widely across industries.

cosy-blockquote.p: Inflation ≠ stability – a general increase in prices and fall in purchasing power.

p.em: Example: High inflation erodes the real value of fixed pensions.

cosy-blockquote.p: Identity ≠ obscurity – the characteristics defining who a person is.

p.em: Example: Many professionals struggle when their job identity ends.

cosy-blockquote.p: Purpose ≠ apathy – the reason for which something is done or created.

p.em: Example: Finding a daily purpose is crucial for healthy aging.

cosy-blockquote.p: Anxiety ≠ calmness – a feeling of worry, nervousness, or unease.

p.em: Example: Financial anxiety can shadow early retirement dreams.

cosy-blockquote.p: Longevity ≠ brevity – long life or long existence.

p.em: Example: Increased longevity means retirement savings must last longer.

cosy-blockquote.p: Contribution ≠ consumption – giving time, money, or effort to a common cause.

p.em: Example: Senior citizens make valuable community contributions.

cosy-blockquote.p: Lifestyle ≠ isolation – the way in which a person or group lives.

p.em: Example: Maintaining an active lifestyle supports cognitive health.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How can working professionals build long-term financial security for post-career life?
★ How early in life did you start thinking about long-term investments?

What features make a private pension plan effective against market volatility?
★ Do you trust private pension funds or state retirement systems?

How does rising inflation affect the purchasing power of fixed retirement incomes?
★ How has recent price inflation changed your spending habits?

How does retiring alter an individual's sense of professional identity and status?
★ Is your job a central part of how you define yourself?

How can retirees find a meaningful purpose after leaving the workforce?
★ What non-work goals give you a sense of fulfillment?

Why do some individuals experience post-retirement anxiety or depression?
★ How do you handle sudden transitions in life?

How does increasing human longevity impact state retirement funds globally?
★ At what age do you realistically hope to retire?

How can retired seniors make valuable societal contributions through volunteering?
★ Have you participated in community volunteering?

What major adjustments are required to maintain a high-quality lifestyle in retirement?
★ What aspect of your lifestyle would you never want to give up?

How does early retirement impact long-term mental sharpness and cognitive health?
★ Would you prefer to work part-time indefinitely rather than full retirement?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Achieving complete financial security is becoming impossible for younger generations. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Are you confident about your economic future?

Relying solely on a state pension plan is a risky financial decision today. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you manage personal investments?

Persistent global inflation will force future generations to work past seventy. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Expecting retirement ages to rise further?

Losing one's career identity causes identity crisis for passionate workers. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you feel lost without your daily job role?

Discovering a strong personal purpose is more important than accumulating wealth. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Value passion or financial gain more?

Overcoming retirement anxiety requires careful psychological preparation before leaving work. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Discuss life transitions with mentors or therapists?

Extended human longevity will make traditional full-stop retirement obsolete. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would phased part-time work suit you better?

Older adults make more significant civic contributions through mentoring than young workers. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Value senior mentorship in your field?

Maintaining an active social lifestyle protects seniors against cognitive decline. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you maintain your social circle?

Planning for post-work life retirement should start during one's very first job. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Should financial literacy be taught in high school?

ul.li: Incorrect: If I will save money, I will retire early. → Correct: If I save money, I will retire early. ((Use present simple in the 'if' condition clause, not 'will'.))
Incorrect: Retirement depends from economic growth. → Correct: Retirement depends on economic growth. ((Preposition rule: 'depend' collocates with 'on', not 'from'.))
